title: Choose the visual world
question: Fresh hand. The roll assigned the Coffee Lot Label. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll again.

options.label: Coffee Lot Label
options.lineage: third-wave specialty roaster bags, lot labels, and SCA cupping forms
options.thesis: Each build is labelled like a specialty coffee lot; NDA work is cupped blind, with the origin withheld and judged on what is in the cup.
materials: flat matte bag colors, one per lot
die-cut paper labels with rubber-stamped dates
options.viewport: One large house label: name as roaster, 'senior full stack, roasting since 2017', origin Philippines (remote), stack as tasting notes, and the Email action as the label's order line.
options.risk: One step from the 'turns coffee into code' cliché, and can make the hobby lead the engineer; bags must stay flat and saturated or they drift into beige craft.

raised.raise: One hot color, one job: vermilion marks only the Email action and the live 'open to work' state.
Calm at rest: the page holds still until touched, and motion only answers the visitor.
Now is always marked: one current-roast line says what is live (available, building Notifly).
Real web technique: moving from lot to lot uses genuine view transitions, not a static imitation.
One claim per label: every lot carries exactly one headline claim.

regions.label: house label: name, role, origin, notes

options.label: Transit Diagram
options.lineage: Manila LRT/MRT and Tokyo Metro route diagrams
options.thesis: The stack as a rail network: the React and Vue lines interchange at TypeScript, and every build is a station you can alight at.
options.viewport: The network fills the first viewport, with the name set as the system's title and Email as the terminus.
options.risk: The skills subway map is a familiar developer-portfolio trope, so it needs real routing to avoid looking like everyone's.

options.label: Warm Consumer App Surface
options.thesis: The portfolio as a calm, friendly app: soft cards, plain words, and one action color only where you can act.
options.viewport: A greeting card with name and role, the Email button as the only bright color, and cards for each build below.
options.case: Holds product clarity (actions are unmistakable) but loses audience identification: it is the generic template you ruled out.
options.risk: Lands on the 'generic dev template' you said would feel wrong.

options.label: Raku Smoke Flash
options.thesis: Builds fired in smoke, cracked glaze on soot.
options.viewport: A soot-black vessel with one ember-hot region.
options.case: Loses both axes: no tie to this audience or the engineering case.
options.kept: Ember reserved for the live state.

options.label: Bioluminescent Wake
options.thesis: Pointer trails light up a black field.
options.viewport: A dark field the cursor paints in blue light.
options.case: Loses both axes: it is the neon-on-black look you called hacker cosplay.

options.label: Drum Machine Step Row
options.thesis: Career years as sixteen step keys under a chase light.
options.viewport: A sixteen-step row with builds armed as lit keys.
options.case: Loses both axes: an instrument toy that hides the hiring case.

options.label: WebGL Shader Portal
options.thesis: A living shader field with thin type floating over it.
options.viewport: A full-screen shader behind a percentage loader.
options.case: Loses both axes: it hides the offer behind a loader and claims a WebGL specialty the owner does not.

options.label: Linocut Broadside
options.thesis: Each build carved as one demand on newsprint.
options.viewport: A monumental gouged figure over carved lettering.
options.case: Loses both axes: protest-print voice does not fit a hiring portfolio.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The senior developer portfolio as the category ships it, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name and role headline, short intro, Email button, selected work below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other dev portfolio by design.
